explanation: Mark every encountered value. A repeated mark identifies the duplicate; the unmarked position identifies the missing value. Return them in that order.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Only a constant number of full input/range scans is needed.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. Presence-array variants allocate n flags; XOR variants retain only a few accumulators.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: After scanning, seen[v] records whether v occurred. Exactly one repeated mark identifies the duplicated value, and the sole unmarked value in 0..n−1 is the missing value. Returning (duplicate,missing) follows the required ordering.
walkthrough: For [0,4,2,4,1], the second 4 sets duplicate=4. The marks for 0,1,2,4 are present but mark 3 is absent, so return (4,3).
edgeCases: The duplicate can appear before the missing value’s expected position.
Zero may be either the duplicated or missing value.
The input contract requires exactly one duplicate and one missing member of 0..n−1.
